Hannah leans in, voice low. "Here's what we figured out about The Living Wire. Get OUT of the water. When the crackling starts, step onto dry ground — the discharge cannot reach you there. On land it is just a long blind fish: slow, harmless, dinner. Never fight it standing in the creek."

💡 COUNTER LEARNED — The Living Wire: Get OUT of the water. When the crackling starts, step onto dry ground — the discharge cannot reach you there. On land it is just a long blind fish: slow, harmless, dinner. Never fight it standing in the creek. (Someone at the haven knew the trick.)

🔥 The fire settles. Joshua has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "Bulldozer — I put it down today." "Lowers its head, paws the earth. Dust rises. It is not going around the tree. It has never gone around anything." "It stops. Blood on its snout, sides heaving. It has decided you are not worth dying for — it backs away, quills flat." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Gerald asks "We've been walking past those." Ivy breathes "Say that again — slower." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"
